Thanks Marissa — quick clarifications before we hand over sample docs:

1) JSON schema compliance: do you enforce schema at the runtime level or is it an eval-time check? We need deterministic guarantees for downstream regulatory ingestion. How do you handle partial/invalid outputs? Is there an automatic retry or fallback to a more reliable model variant?

2) Tool/function calling: we saw references to callable validators — will those be run synchronously as part of the request or as a post-processing step? Any latency considerations?

3) Retries & idempotency: if the model returns malformed JSON, what's your recommended retry strategy (prompt-engineered retry vs simply switching model/params)? Do you include any idempotency tokens or request hashes to protect downstream side effects?

If you can call these out I can prioritize the sample documents that stress those cases.

Hi Samir — answering inline:

1) Schema compliance
- We treat schema validation as a first-class eval and provide two levels:
  a) Eval-time scoring: your canonical schema is used to score outputs (JSON schema validation + soft checks like field types/format)
  b) Runtime enforcement (optional): we can apply a lightweight post-processing validator that rejects responses failing strict schema checks and either retries the model with a schema-priming prompt or routes to a more robust model variant.

Behaviour on invalid outputs
- Default: we return the raw model output and surface validation findings in the response metadata (validation.errors array in the SDK response)
- Optional strict mode: runtime rejects and triggers a retry loop (configurable attempts, backoff). In strict mode you can choose:
  • Retry with same model + schema-primed prompt (cheap, often works for missing commas/close-braces)
  • Failover to a higher-quality model (e.g., redwood-7b-int8 -> open-llama-13b-quant)

2) Tool/function calling
- Tool calls are synchronous by default in our hosted API: the model returns a function call token, we execute the function (validator) and feed results back into a short context window for a final output. This adds a small latency delta (typically 30–120ms depending on validator complexity).
- You can also run validators as async post-processing (recommended for heavy validation or external system checks).

3) Retries & idempotency
- We recommend a layered strategy:
  • First retry: prompt-engineered re-ask (schema-primed). Include request_id in conversation metadata.
  • Second: failover to a more capable model variant.
  • For side-effecting operations, use idempotency tokens (we pass an idempotency key header in SDK calls) so downstream systems can de-duplicate.

Testing suggestions
- Provide 50–100 labeled examples covering edge cases; we'll run structured-output evals and produce a precision/recall table per field.
- Include fuzzed inputs that break formatting to test recovery heuristics.

Attaching a sample eval result (sample_eval_results.json) from a prior run so you can see the validator output fields.
